item.title: Higgs Fluctuation Solver in Four Dimensions: Part II-Toward Finite Lattice-to-MS bar Matching in the SU(2) Higgs Extension
item.description: arXiv:2611.26780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a lattice-to-MS_bar matching framework for the $SU(2)$-Higgs theory, including Wilson-plaquette and fundamental scalar-link actions, a counter term basis through $\rho^{12}$, audited momentum-dependent lattice vertices, and fixed routings and projectors. At the benchmark $a=0.8$, $m_0^2=\mu_R^2=0.4$, $g_0=0.65$, and $(\lambda,\gamma,\delta)=(-2,0.8,0.08)$, the potential is $V_0(\rho)=\frac{1}{5}\rho^2-\frac{1}{2}\rho^4+\frac{2}{15}\rho^6+\frac{1}{100}\rho^8$. The scalar-only radial matching shifts, ordered as $(\delta m^2,\delta\lambda,\delta\gamma,\delta\delta,\delta c_{10},\delta c_{12})$, are $(2.75293, -1.45119, -2.85120, 0.356724, 1.07432, 6.20492)$ in solver units, with the continuum-renormalized-minus-lattice convention. The Higgs two-point slope gives $\delta Z_H = 0.0329117974 \pm 0.00000036$ (QMC error). We also evaluate gauge-linked four-, six-, and eight-Higgs projections and derive the continuum one-loop gauge two-point tensor. The tensor passes 29 internal checks; at $p^2=0.4$, its total transverse projection is $\Pi_T=-0.01847$ at zero regulator and $-0.01716$ at $\lambda_{\mathrm{IR}}/\mu_R=1/8$, while the regulator-induced longitudinal projection is $\Pi_L=1.04\times 10^{-5}$ at $\lambda_{\mathrm{IR}}/\mu_R=1/32$. These results establish a tested foundation and quantitative benchmarks for the matching program. The gauge-linked projections remain preliminary, and full gauge-sector matching and Ward-Slavnov-Taylor closure are needed before a matched $SU(2)$ decay prefactor can be claimed.
item.dc:creator: Merritt S. Cook

item.title: Optimized solver algorithms for computing $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$
item.description: arXiv:2611.26854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Estimating the trace of the inverse of a large quark matrix is a longstanding problem in lattice QCD. The standard approach is Hutchinson's method, which uses random noise vectors to estimate the trace to a desired statistical tolerance. Each noise vector $b$ requires solving a system of linear equations $Ax = b$. In this work, we introduce a new class of Krylov solvers for this task, called Twin methods. Twin methods generate the Krylov polynomial once then reuse it on all other right-hand sides. This reduces the number of basic linear algebra operations in the algorithm and therefore lowers the trace computation time. We apply the Twin approach to BiCG and BiCGStab and test them on lattice QCD matrices of varying size and in a range of computing contexts. We also present a more economical estimation of $\mathrm{Tr}(A^{-1})$ which implements a polynomial approximation of $A^{-1}$ and a singular value deflation. In this scheme, the solvers are applied to only a few noise vectors, and the remainder are treated by the polynomial and the deflation. In our tests, the polynomial approximation combined with the deflation yield a 17-fold speedup in the time required to compute the trace over standard Hutchinson's method.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Luke, Sudip Shiwakoti, Shayan Nadeem, Ronald Morgan, Walter Wilcox

item.title: Numerical tests of 5D APS $\eta$-invariant phases for 4D chiral fermions
item.description: arXiv:2611.27307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We calculate the phase of a 4D chiral fermion determinant from the 5D Atiyah--Patodi--Singer (APS) $\eta$-invariant. We study the anomaly-free $SU(5)$ representation $\mathbf{10}\oplus\overline{\mathbf 5}$ on a four-torus, using gauge fields independent of one coordinate. For these backgrounds, the 4D phase can be calculated independently from a 3D Dirac spectrum. For an Abelian background embedded in $SU(5)$, two different 5D bulk extensions reproduce the 4D phase within $0.03\%$ in the tested heat-kernel extrapolations. One extension changes the spatial gauge field along the fifth direction and requires a coupled 5D spectral calculation. An independent single-charge check reproduces the Chern--Simons anomaly coefficient within $0.3\%$ using quadratic extrapolations. We also calculate 5D APS phases for non-Abelian backgrounds in the $SU(4)\times U(1)$ subgroup. For a background generating the full $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ algebra, the 5D phase with a fixed spatial field agrees with the independent 4D phase within $0.5\%$ over the six heat-kernel parameters examined. We further study a varying-field 5D extension for an embedded $SU(2)$ background. These results show that the 5D APS calculation reproduces a nonzero chiral phase after anomaly cancellation.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuhiro Misumi

item.title: From Resonance Properties to High-Energy Behavior: The $R$ Ratio from Lattice QCD
item.description: arXiv:2611.27586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate resonance properties and inclusive spectral behavior through Bayesian reconstruction of the $R$-ratio from Euclidean lattice correlators near the physical pion mass. Without additional Gaussian smearing, the reconstructed spectrum already captures the smooth high-energy behavior observed in experiment. Direct integration of the $\rho$ peak determines $f_\rho$ with approximately $1\%$ statistical precision and close agreement with the experimental reference, providing access to resonance properties without resolving individual finite-volume levels. With a common Gaussian width of $\sigma=0.6$~GeV, the lattice and experimental $R$-ratios show good overall agreement over $0.25$--$2.50$~GeV. Comparisons among ensembles with spatial extents up to approximately $10$~fm demonstrate that finite-volume effects can be controlled across these complementary observables. These results demonstrate a unified framework for studying resonance and inclusive physics from lattice QCD, with potential applications to other hadronic channels, inclusive decay rates, and hadronic tensors.
item.dc:creator: Nan Wang, Long-cheng Gui, Jun Hua, Jian Liang, Keh-Fei Liu, Jun Shi, Gen Wang

item.title: Solving fermionic sign problems with physics-informed kernels
item.description: arXiv:2611.27768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the generative sampling approach with physics-informed kernels (PIKs) [1,2] to a general class of physics systems with complex distributions and a structure also encountered in fermionic systems. The resolution of sign problems of generic weighted sums of complex Gau{\ss}ian distributions with the PIK approach is central to this application. In a first step, PIKs map a real normal distribution to such a weighted sum, and this procedure is called the PIKfan. The PIKfan has the sampling cost of a real normal distribution. In a second step, this weighted sum is evolved with a second PIK into the distribution of the theory at hand. In combination, we reduce the sampling task for a general class of complex systems to a Gau{\ss}ian one, and the main computational task is that of computing the PIK. We illustrate the approach with the one-site Hubbard model at arbitrary chemical potential and with $\phi^4$-deformed extensions of it.
item.dc:creator: Kenji Fukushima, Friederike Ihssen, Renzo Kapust, Jan M. Pawlowski

item.title: Sampling non-abelian lattice gauge theories with diffusion models
item.description: arXiv:2611.27821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present gauge-equivariant diffusion models as samplers for lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Using lattice gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs) and the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), we are able to accurately sample two-dimensional U(2) field configurations and show first promising results for four-dimensional SU(3). Our two-dimensional models extrapolate remarkably well to larger inverse couplings than originally trained on. We confirm this by comparing observables to analytically known values and to hybrid Monte Carlo results.
item.dc:creator: Gert Aarts, Diaa E. Habibi, Andreas Ipp, David I. M\"uller, Thomas R. Ranner, Lingxiao Wang, Wei Wang, Qianteng Zhu

item.title: Thermalization and quantum chaos in a pure gauge discrete non-Abelian lattice gauge theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.26695v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gauge theories constitute the basis of our microscopic description of fundamental physical laws, and they are a cornerstone of contemporary scientific research. Yet, how such systems thermalize far from equilibrium remains a fundamental open question at the crossroads of statistical, high-energy, and condensed-matter physics. In this work, we investigate the thermalization properties of non-Abelian lattice gauge theories, focusing on the discrete gauge group $D_3$, which is ideally suited for current qudit-based quantum simulators. Specifically, we study a linear plaquette chain in a gauge-fixed formulation that removes unphysical degrees of freedom. A numerical analysis of the Hamiltonian spectrum and expectation values of local operators shows a behavior broadly aligned with the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH). We also study thermalization through the real-time dynamics of the entanglement spectrum, confirming the emergence of random-matrix level statistics after an initial transient. Our results expand the rich phenomenology of dihedral non-Abelian gauge systems. Once the relevant symmetry structure is properly resolved, the model displays the same qualitative ETH-based thermalization scenario observed in Abelian gauge models and generic non-integrable quantum many-body systems.
item.dc:creator: Marco Vaia, Edoardo Ballini, Alberto Bottarelli, Matteo M. Wauters, Philipp Hauke

item.title: Evidence for Y-shaped color confinement of fully heavy baryons
item.description: arXiv:2611.27014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The geometry of color confinement in baryons remains a fundamental question in quantum chromodynamics. We investigate whether heavy-quark spectroscopy can distinguish a genuine three-body Y-shaped confining interaction from a sum of pairwise $\Delta$-shaped interaction. Using a high-precision three-body Schr\"odinger solver, we perform a simultaneous analysis of experimentally measured bottomonium masses and lattice-QCD calculations of $\Omega_{bbb}$ excitation energies. For each confinement scenario, interaction parameters are independently optimized against the combined spectra. We find that the Y-shaped potential provides a consistent description of both systems, whereas the $\Delta$-shaped potential exhibits significant discrepancies. Our results provide spectroscopic evidence favoring a collective three-body confining interaction and establish triply-heavy baryon spectroscopy as a complementary probe of the nonperturbative geometry of color confinement.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxing Zhao, Shuzhe Shi, Pengfei Zhuang

item.title: String breaking in a (1+1)-dimensional $e^+e^-$ collider
item.description: arXiv:2611.27134v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we develop a framework for studying solitons in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories using tensor networks, and we apply it to simulate $e^+e^-$ collisions in the massive Schwinger model. We work at $\theta = \pi$ and at a bare fermion mass exceeding the critical value; in this regime, there are two degenerate vacua, and the $e^+$ and $e^-$ particles are realized as soliton states interpolating between them. We carefully explain how to find and characterize such soliton states using infinite tensor network methods, and then exhibit real-time simulations of their collisions. These collisions involve the formation of an energetic flux string, and we demonstrate that our final states are superpositions of elastic and string-breaking trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Ross Dempsey, Anna-Maria E. Gl\"uck, Silviu S. Pufu, Benjamin T. S{\o}gaard

item.title: Quark dipole operators in the gradient-flow scheme at NNLO QCD
item.description: arXiv:2611.27708v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conversion factors for the dimension-five QCD operator basis from the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ to the gradient-flow scheme are presented through NNLO in the strong coupling. In the CP-even sector, the results are provided for general quark masses and arbitrary flavor content of the operators. Specifically, this concerns the quark CMDM operator and its mixing with lower-dimensional QCD operators. In the massless case, our results immediately apply to the quark chromoelectric dipole operator. As a by-product, we also determine missing entries in the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ anomalous dimension matrix of the CMDM operator to NNLO QCD.
item.dc:creator: Janosch Borgulat, Lars Georg, Robert V. Harlander, Jonas T. Kohnen, Andrea Shindler

item.title: Optimised 8th-Order Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Quantum Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27896v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulating quantum dynamics in many-body systems is one of the most promising applications of quantum computers. Product formulas are a natural choice for this task, since they map directly onto quantum gates, and increasing their order $n$ could lead to reduced gate depths, provided the parameters are chosen efficiently. So far, schemes beyond $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order have only been built as compositions of second-order schemes, while more general product formulas are known only up to $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order. In this work, we extend our optimisation framework to order $n = 8$, and find both more efficient compositions and the first $8^{\textrm{th}}$ order general schemes. Our formulas improve on the theoretical efficiency of the state-of-the-art schemes by Morales et al and we recommend two schemes explicitly. In simulations of the Heisenberg XZ chain one of our recommended schemes always outperforms those by Morales et al, though it is not always the same scheme that performs best. More generally, we observe that for Hamiltonians split into many non-commuting operators the uniformity of a Trotter decomposition becomes the main indicator of a scheme's performance. To assess the schemes' use on quantum hardware, we simulate noisy circuits with our new Qiskit plugin qiskit-omelyan. At current noise levels, the Leapfrog scheme remains the best choice, but as noise rates decrease toward fault tolerance, our recommended schemes become competitive.
item.dc:creator: Marko Male\v{z}i\v{c}, Johann Ostmeyer

item.title: Lattice QCD determination of the $\gamma Z$ box contribution to the proton weak charge
item.description: arXiv:2601.06582v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the first lattice QCD determination of the $\gamma Z$ box contribution to parity-violating electron-proton scattering, $\square_{\gamma Z}$, a key ingredient for the precise tests of the Standard Model via the proton weak charge. Our calculation covers the electron beam energies up to $E=155$ MeV. At $E=0$, the vector contribution is known analytically and excluded by convention; for the remaining axial-vector component we obtain $\square_{\gamma Z}(0)=0.00411(9)$. Incorporating this result implies a value for weak charge of $Q_W^p=0.06987(50)$. The calculated energy dependence of $\square_{\gamma Z}$ is directly relevant to the upcoming P2 experiment at Mainz, which will operate at the optimized beam energy of 155 MeV to extract $Q_W^p$.Although the systematic error budget in this exploratory study is not yet complete, this work establishes a lattice-QCD framework for computing the $\gamma Z$ box contribution and demonstrates the feasibility of a first-principles approach, providing a foundation for future calculations with improved systematic control.
item.dc:creator: Zhao-long Zhang, Xu Feng, Mikhail Gorchtein, Lu-Chang Jin, Chuan Liu, Chien-Yeah Seng

item.title: Electromagnetic pion mass splitting using a Pauli-Villars-regulated photon propagator
item.description: arXiv:2605.29902v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a lattice QCD calculation of the charged-neutral pion mass splitting $M_{\pi^+} - M_{\pi^0}$ at $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_\mathrm{em})$ using a recently proposed framework based on a Pauli-Villars (PV) regulated photon propagator defined in the continuum and infinite-volume limit, with $\Lambda$ acting as an additional UV cutoff scale. This formulation, when combined with a dedicated treatment of the elastic contribution, avoids power-law finite-volume effects on electromagnetic mass shifts. We perform the calculation using CLS ensembles, studying finite-volume effects, the continuum limit and the extrapolation to the physical point for several values of the scale $\Lambda$. By means of the Cottingham formula, we further decompose the result into elastic and inelastic contributions at fixed $\Lambda$. Our final result, after removing the cutoff scale $\Lambda$, is $M_{\pi^+} - M_{\pi^0} = 4.56(22)$ MeV, in good agreement with the experimental measurement. Our complete calculation demonstrates that, for a mass splitting not requiring any counterterms, the formalism can be implemented successfully, whilst also offering useful insights into the computation of electromagnetic corrections to other observables.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro De Santis, Dominik Erb, Harvey B. Meyer

item.title: Operator Learning for Spectral Reconstruction from Euclidean Correlators
item.description: arXiv:2607.03311v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we propose a novel supervised machine-learning-based strategy for extracting smeared spectral functions from Euclidean correlation functions. The strategy revisits the numerically ill-posed spectral reconstruction problem within the framework of Operator Learning through the use of DeepONet-like architectures. To illustrate the method, we construct an ensemble of neural networks trained on mock data generated from Gaussian Processes containing different levels of prior knowledge. This ensemble is then employed to estimate the systematic uncertainty associated with the fact that a neural network provides only an approximation to the target operator. The procedure is fully validated on previously unseen noisy mock data. To demonstrate the potential of the method for phenomenological applications, we reconstruct the inclusive rate above the four-particle threshold and up to high energies in the $1+1$-dimensional O(3) non-linear $\sigma$ model, starting from correlation functions computed in Monte Carlo simulations. The final result is consistent with the known analytic spectral density and, compared with the state-of-the-art Hansen-Lupo-Tantalo algorithm, exhibits a significant reduction in the total uncertainty even under mild physical assumptions encoded in the training set. The proposed strategy can be naturally extended to more phenomenologically relevant observables in lattice QCD.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro De Santis

item.title: Information geometry of continuum limits in lattice field theory: The Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34277v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When the Boltzmann weight is nonnegative, the actions of a lattice field theory form a statistical manifold, whose Fisher metric gives the number of measurements needed to distinguish two nearby actions. For the two-dimensional lattice Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions in the large-$N$ limit, we study the continuum limit, in which the lattice spacing $a$ goes to zero at fixed mass gap $\Lambda$, through the Fisher metric of the distribution of the auxiliary field $\sigma$. The renormalization condition fixes an expectation coordinate, and dimensional transmutation becomes an exponential relation between it and a natural coordinate. The main result is that the $a\to0$ limits differ between the Fisher metric of the long-distance modes, whose momenta are fixed in physical units, and that of the full $P(\sigma)$. In the former, the infinitely many irrelevant directions that change the kinetic term locally shrink relative to the mass-term direction to order $a\Lambda\log(1/(a\Lambda))$ or smaller, and several modes together leave only the two directions $(\Lambda,m)$ of the continuum theory. In the latter, the kinetic-term directions shrink as fast as the mass-term direction, and the difference in the regularization remains in lattice-scale correlations. In the eight-dimensional space of local deformations examined numerically, the one exception is the deformation that only adds a contact term to the propagator, which as $a\to0$ becomes indistinguishable from a change of $1/g^2$ in both metrics. In the Fisher metric of the full $P(\sigma)$, the curvature of the coupling plane at fixed kinetic term diverges as $(1/2)\log^2(1/(a\Lambda))$, not as the correlation volume often assumed in thermodynamic geometry, and the critical point lies at infinite distance in this plane.
item.dc:creator: Akio Tomiya

item.title: Efficient Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Long-time Quantum Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2601.18756v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurately simulating long-time dynamics of many-body systems is a challenge in both classical and quantum computing due to the accumulation of Trotter errors. While low-order Trotter-Suzuki decompositions are straightforward to implement, their rapidly growing error limits access to long-time observables. We present a framework for constructing efficient high-order Trotter-Suzuki schemes by identifying their structure and directly optimizing their parameters over a high-dimensional space. This method enables the discovery of new schemes with significantly improved efficiency compared to traditional constructions, such as those by Suzuki and Yoshida. Based on the theoretical efficiency and practical performance, we recommend two novel highly efficient schemes at $4^{\textrm{th}}$ and $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of these decompositions on the Heisenberg model and the quantum harmonic oscillator, and find that for a fixed final time they perform better across the computational cost. Even when using large time steps, they surpass established low-order schemes like the Leapfrog. Finally, we investigate the in-practice performance of different Trotter schemes and find the decompositions with more uniform coefficients tend to feature improved error accumulation over long times. We have included this observation into our choice of recommended schemes.
item.dc:creator: Marko Male\v{z}i\v{c}, Johann Ostmeyer

item.title: From Self-Dual to Physical $\mathbb{C}P^{N-1}$: Anomalies, Boundary Stokes Phenomenon, and Global Structure of $\theta$-vacua
item.description: arXiv:2608.30160v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a two-coupling generalization of $\mathbb{C}P^{N-1}$ model that continuously interpolates between the self-dual ($\epsilon=0$) and the physical ($\epsilon=g$) theories as a useful nonperturbative tool. At $\epsilon \neq g$, this model possesses a chiral imbalance, which may be viewed as a real topological deformation (imaginary-$\theta$). We demonstrate that exact quantum equivalence between first- and second-order formulations strictly requires a topological counterterm sourced by a bosonic chiral anomaly. Solving this deformed theory at large $N$ yields two primary results. First, we analytically determine the nonperturbative vacuum structure of the self-dual theory, a self-dual vacuum with a dynamically generated field-strength condensate. Second, we resolve a fundamental paradox where saddles with $(\theta + 2\pi n) \sim O(N)$ ($n$ is branch number) spuriously yield lower energy densities than the physical ground state. Because the effective action possesses an essential singularity at $F=0$, we show that the Lefschetz thimble analysis must be generalized to include boundary thimbles. A boundary Stokes phenomenon renders the problematic saddles topologically inactive, fully restoring the validity of the large-$N$ expansion for strongly coupled theories.
item.dc:creator: Yui Hayashi, Mithat \"{U}nsal

item.title: Examples of infinitesimal Gribov copies in the presence of planar boundaries, and an emergent boundary gauge invariance in Yang-Mills theory
item.description: arXiv:2608.30447v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: First, we explicitly construct zero-modes of the Yang-Mills Faddeev-Popov operator in the presence of two parallel plates, with either perfect electric (PEC) or perfect magnetic (PMC) boundary conditions imposed. This establishes the existence of infinitesimal Gribov copies with finite action, and even finite L_2-norm, in Yang-Mills theory with non-trivial interfaces. We adapt Henyey's construction, although the boundary configuration imposes extra restrictions on the ansatz for the gauge field. Second, we discuss the phenomenon of an emergent boundary gauge invariance for PEC and PMC plates in Yang-Mills theory. This shall be important when applying the Gribov-Zwanziger procedure to parallel plate setups, of relevance for non-perturbatively studying the non-Abelian Casimir effect in the future.
item.dc:creator: David Dudal, Luigi Rosa, Sebbe Stouten

item.title: Casimir effect in Gribov-Zwanziger theory
item.description: arXiv:2609.11448v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider Yang-Mills theory with two infinite parallel plates, separated by a distance \(L\), that are perfect magnetic conductors (PMC) or perfect electric conductors (PEC). Recently, it was shown that the Gribov copy problem persists in such a setting. We then study the Gribov-Zwanziger (GZ) action in the presence of those boundaries using functional integral methods. Lagrange multiplier fields allow one to lift the boundary conditions into the action, after which the boundary modifications to the gluon propagator can straightforwardly be determined. In the PEC case, we provide evidence that, even when translation invariance is (partially) broken, the usual horizon term in the GZ action still restricts the functional integral to the Gribov region. We compute the Casimir energy for GZ with PMC or PEC plates, both directly from the functional integral and from the energy-momentum tensor, obtaining consistent results. We compare our analytical results with recent lattice data, in both 4D and 3D. A priori, one might expect that the boundary-modified gluon propagator introduces new \(L\)-dependencies into the GZ gap equation. This would make the Gribov mass \(\gamma\) dynamically dependent on \(L\), implying an interesting interplay with the Casimir energy. However, we show that no such dynamical \(L\)-dependence occurs within the current approximation.
item.dc:creator: David Dudal, Philipe De Fabritiis, Sebbe Stouten, David Vercauteren

item.title: The index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators: I
item.description: arXiv:2611.08266v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This is the first of a series of papers which will be devoted to a study of the index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on closed Riemannian manifolds. The aim of the series is to discretise the index of the Dirac operator. On flat tori, this is achieved by the Wilson--Dirac operator of lattice gauge theory on a regular lattice. On a general closed Riemannian manifold, however, no regular lattice is available. As an intermediate step between the continuum Dirac operator and its discretisations, we introduce mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on any closed Riemannian manifold, defined by integrating covariant differences over distances comparable to a fixed length scale. In this paper, we define the index of the mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators via spectral flow and prove that it agrees with that of the continuum Dirac operator at all sufficiently small scales. The proof rests on an elliptic estimate uniform in the scale and a Rellich-type compactness theorem. In the second paper, we shall pass from mesoscopic operators to discrete Wilson--Dirac operators.
item.dc:creator: Mikio Furuta, Shinichiroh Matsuo
